rewritten_query:
select count(*) from (
  select distinct c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date
  from store_sales, date_dim, customer
  where store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
    and store_sales.ss_customer_sk = customer.c_customer_sk
    and d_month_seq between 1215 and 1226
    and c_birth_month in (3, 6, 7, 8)
    and ss_list_price between 241 and 300
    and ss_wholesale_cost between 45 and 65
  intersect
  select distinct c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date
  from catalog_sales, date_dim, customer
  where catalog_sales.cs_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
    and catalog_sales.cs_bill_customer_sk = customer.c_customer_sk
    and d_month_seq between 1215 and 1226
    and c_birth_month in (3, 6, 7, 8)
    and cs_list_price between 241 and 300
    and cs_wholesale_cost between 45 and 65
  intersect
  select distinct c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date
  from web_sales, date_dim, customer
  where web_sales.ws_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
    and web_sales.ws_bill_customer_sk = customer.c_customer_sk
    and d_month_seq between 1215 and 1226
    and c_birth_month in (3, 6, 7, 8)
    and ws_list_price between 241 and 300
    and ws_wholesale_cost between 45 and 65
) hot_cust;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Fold the date expression '1215 + 11' into the constant 1226 to remove per-row arithmetic.
Remove the outer 'limit 100': count(*) returns a single row, so the LIMIT is ineffective and adds no value.

Keep the INTERSECT structure: converting to INNER JOINs risks semantic differences because INTERSECT treats NULLs as equal while join '=' does not; the set operation itself is not a bottleneck (the cost is dominated by the per-branch fact-table scans).
